world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Stormbay, necromancy is forbidden; in Cinder Cliff, it is permitted; in Headlandharbor, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Scholars debate in public courtyards, while the rural shrines keep older traditions alive.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Neighbors exchange handmade gifts and tell stories of the year.

rumors: The academy in Stormbay is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Fernsong Thicket can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Discreet physicians preserve ancestral knowledge despite the ban.
Makers are needed along the road to The Sun Arch Keep; honest craft can become a life’s work.
Harbor workers argue over storm repairs and the price of inland grain.
The ferrymen call the water Gallows Beck; its old crossing bells can still be heard after dusk.

journal.title: A life begins at birth
journal.text: Isven Terassi was born in Stormbay to a freeholder family. The morning brought driving rain.

journal.title: A Small Beginning
journal.text: Haldis Terassi chooses to keep the door closed.

journal.title: A Low Note
journal.text: A low hum is easier to follow than speech. For a little while, each breath seems to carry the same note through the dark.

journal.title: A need your life can make room for
journal.text: A wound infection: Tenderness, fatigue, and a wound that needs cleaning. Free care and supportive choices remain available.

journal.title: A World of Breathing
journal.text: For now, the world comes as warmth, hunger and the rise and fall of nearby breathing. Beyond it, Stormbay has names you cannot yet know.

journal.title: Care around your earliest days
journal.text: The adults caring for you made room for 3 days of rest and comfort. Familiar hands and voices stayed close while you recovered. No payment came from your belongings.

journal.title: A period of recovery
journal.text: A wound infection eased after lived time and care. This experience remains in your history; recurring symptoms can still ask for support later.

journal.title: The Small Hours
journal.text: You wake while the world is quiet, then drift away before it has finished waking. The hours belong to bodily needs rather than bells or promises.

journal.title: A Song Before Sleep
journal.text: Haldis Terassi chooses to put the song away.

journal.title: No Name for Morning
journal.text: The dark thins. Sounds begin again, one after another. You have no name for morning; it arrives all the same, asking only that you wake.

journal.title: Before Words
journal.text: A voice repeats the same soft sounds. You do not know the story inside them; you know the pause before the voice begins again.

journal.title: The Edge of Cloth
journal.text: Your fingers close around a fold of cloth. The rough weave, the warmth beneath it and the effort of holding on fill the whole moment.

journal.title: Your First Words
journal.text: Haldis Terassi chooses to write down the unfamiliar word.

journal.title: Steps Beyond Sight
journal.text: Footsteps pass somewhere beyond your view: near, then far, then gone. You turn toward the sound before there is a word for where it went.

journal.title: Light on the Wall
journal.text: A patch of light moves beyond your reach. Your eyes follow it until it breaks into shadow. No kingdom could be larger than that wall today.

journal.title: The Returning Shape
journal.text: A familiar shape leans close, disappears and returns. You cannot count the returns, but your body knows the difference between waiting and being held.

journal.title: A Broken Cup
journal.text: You take the blame.

journal.title: Between the City Sounds
journal.text: At Stormbay, one sound rarely ends before another begins. In the gaps, you notice the stone’s colder hush, waiting underneath the life passing over it.

journal.title: The Tallest Door
journal.text: The doorways of Stormbay still belong to taller people. You look up at a worn lintel and wonder how many heads have passed beneath it.

journal.text: You wonder where the dark goes when morning comes. Nothing at Stormbay gives an answer, but the unanswered question feels less frightening in daylight.

journal.text: A knot in wood has the face of a little horned thing from a frightening story. From another angle it looks worried. You wonder whether monsters ever frighten themselves.

journal.title: The Familiar Way of Speaking
journal.text: Haldis Terassi has a familiar rhythm of speech. The words may change, but a pause in just the right place can make an ordinary sentence sound like home.

journal.title: Three knocks beneath the bridge

kin.speaker: kin
kin.text:
Isven Terassi, happy 6th birthday.

I hope this year brings a friend who enjoys your questions. You do not need to know the answer before you are allowed to ask.

I hope I leave room to hear you, instead of always remembering who you were.

My work as a herbalist gives me plenty to think about, but I wanted to make room for your birthday too.

— Haldis Terassi

My work as a herbalist gives me plenty to think about, but I wanted to make room for your birthday too.

entries.title: A Letter from Haldis Terassi
entries.body:
Isven Terassi, happy 6th birthday.

I hope this year brings a friend who enjoys your questions. You do not need to know the answer before you are allowed to ask.

I hope I leave room to hear you, instead of always remembering who you were.

My work as a herbalist gives me plenty to think about, but I wanted to make room for your birthday too.

— Haldis Terassi

entries.title: A Letter from Beddie Amblet
entries.body:
Isven Terassi, happy 6th birthday.

I hope there is still something that makes you forget to count the hours. A good question can be a fine beginning to a year.

There is no debt attached to this letter. I only wanted you to know I was thinking of you.

— Beddie Amblet

entries.title: A Letter from Faska Vornell
entries.body:
Isven Terassi, happy 6th birthday.

I hope this year brings a friend who enjoys your questions. You do not need to know the answer before you are allowed to ask.

We have not always found it easy to speak. I did not want this day to pass without a word; you need not find a reply before you are ready.

— Faska Vornell

entries.title: A Letter from Jarnel Terassi
entries.body:
Isven Terassi, happy 6th birthday.

Do you have a story you want to tell in your own way? It does not need to sound like the version in a book.

I hope we keep a little room for the stories nobody else in the family quite understands.

— Jarnel Terassi

entries.title: A Letter from Haldis Terassi
entries.body:
Isven Terassi, happy 12th birthday.

Growing up seems to bring a great many opinions from other people. Leave a little space among them for your own.

I am still learning how to be your parent as you become your own person.

My work as a herbalist gives me plenty to think about, but I wanted to make room for your birthday too.

— Haldis Terassi

entries.title: A Letter from Beddie Amblet
entries.body:
Isven Terassi, happy 12th birthday.

Growing up seems to bring a great many opinions from other people. Leave a little space among them for your own.

I am glad our paths crossed. I would like to keep hearing where yours is taking you.

— Beddie Amblet

entries.title: A Letter from Faska Vornell
entries.body:
Isven Terassi, happy 12th birthday.

What part of your day do people keep forgetting to ask about? That is the part I would like to hear when you feel like telling it.

We have not always found it easy to speak. I did not want this day to pass without a word; you need not find a reply before you are ready.

— Faska Vornell

entries.title: A Letter from Jarnel Terassi
entries.body:
Isven Terassi, happy 12th birthday.

You are allowed to change your mind as you learn more about yourself. I would rather hear an honest uncertainty than a plan chosen only to please me.

We need not become alike to remain part of one another’s lives.

— Jarnel Terassi
